children: Evommune announced EVO756 Phase 2b in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis did not meet primary or secondary endpoints and will be discontinued for AD.
Phase 2b randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (121 adults) failed to meet primary and secondary endpoints at Week 12.
EVO756 was generally well tolerated, supporting continued evaluation in migraine prophylaxis rather than AD.
Evommune will not advance EVO756 for atopic dermatitis based on these top-line results.
EVO301, the IL-18BP fusion protein, will become the lead AD program with a Phase 2b planned for mid-2027 following positive Phase 2a data.
Company expects current cash, cash equivalents and investments to fund operations into 2029 under revised plans.

title: Evommune: EVO756 Phase 2b in Atopic Dermatitis Fails to Meet Endpoints; Development Ceased for AD
